old: Its deepest root once simply meant the weather and seasons overhead.
It passed through Arabic, Latin, and French before landing as a yearly book of dates.
Related to the Arabic al-munāḵ, the word for 'climate' itself.
clues: This type of annual reference book has a name that traces back to an Arabic word whose older root meant 'climate.'
Published yearly, it pairs the calendar with sunrise times, moon phases, tide tables and weather forecasts, so it is far richer than a plain wall calendar.
Farmers have long consulted the Old Farmer's edition for planting dates and frost predictions, and Benjamin Franklin famously published Poor Richard's version.
